MT-2027-LC138.s: School districts that give ID cards to students in grades 7 through 12 would have to print the 988 suicide and crisis hotline number on the front or back of those cards. The rule would apply to cards printed on or after July 1, 2027. Schools would not have to reprint cards made before that date.

MT-2027-LC240.s: The bill would set rules for choosing, overseeing, and removing Montana commissioners to an Article V convention called to propose U.S. constitutional amendments. It would require commissioners to meet set age, residency, voting, and conflict rules, follow limits in their commission, and take an oath. It would also create a legislative advisory committee to fill vacancies, monitor conduct, and help remove commissioners who go beyond their authority.

MT-2027-LC324.s: The bill would change Montana laws on short-barreled rifles, shotguns, firearms, and silencers. It would remove the ban on hunting with a silencer or muffling device, update state references to silencer registration under federal law, and remove the penalty for having a sawed-off firearm. It would also say the wildlife department may not regulate firearms, firearm accessories, or ammunition, while still allowing some hunting rules and safety limits.

MT-2027-LC347.s: The bill would raise the cap on annual fees for public water supply systems, including the minimum fee and the fee for transient noncommunity water systems. It would affect owners of these systems, and city systems could raise rates to cover the fee costs without a public hearing. The bill would take effect July 1, 2027.

MT-2027-LC364.s: The bill would remove a property tax exemption for money or property held by a legal guardian for an incompetent veteran, meaning a veteran who cannot manage their affairs. It would affect those guardians and any property funded by federal pension, compensation, insurance, adjusted compensation, or gratuity payments. The change would apply to property tax years beginning after December 31, 2027.

MT-2027-LC365.s: The bill would change the state property tax relief program so that eligibility is based on meeting the homestead reduced tax rate rules. It would also make the same application, appeal, and penalty rules apply, and it would tighten penalties for false or fraudulent claims. The changes would affect owners of primary homes that qualify for this tax relief and county tax offices that handle the credits.

MT-2027-LC366.s: The bill would change ballot and notice language for school and local tax elections so people can see the expected property tax impact on a home. It would require estimates for homes worth $100,000, $300,000, $600,000, and the county median home value for a main residence, and it would let a district or local government use a different home value in some cases. It would also require the state revenue department to provide an online tool for calculating the impact and for school districts and other taxing bodies to post that tool on their websites.

MT-2027-LC367.s: Montana would revise the income tax credit for older homeowners and renters. It would raise the income amount used to figure household income, increase the top credit from $1,150 to $1,400, and change the income phaseout levels, with yearly inflation updates for those income limits. The change would take effect when approved and would apply to income tax years after December 31, 2026.

MT-2027-LC368.s: The bill would change how county tax appeal board members file property tax appeals. If a board member files an appeal, it would have to be filed in an adjacent county, and that county’s tax appeal board would review it the same way it reviews other appeals. The change would apply to county tax appeal applications filed on or after the effective date.

MT-2027-LC377.s: The bill would extend the end dates for several laws tied to Montana’s Water Court and water right adjudication. It would keep some current water court process funding and rules in place longer, including changes to the water adjudication account. The bill would take effect on July 1, 2027.

MT-2027-LC378.s: The bill would let some owners of recorded land tracts use a water-right permit exception if they got a state water letter before February 14, 2024, got subdivision approval when needed, and file a notice of completion by January 1, 2032. It would also update Montana water law to spell out when some groundwater uses do not need a permit and how notices and water-right certificates must be filed. The change would take effect right away.

MT-2027-LC380.s: The bill would require the Department of Natural Resources and Conservation to study water right permit and change processes, work with water users and other stakeholders, and suggest ways to make the process faster while still protecting senior water rights. It would also require progress updates during the 2027-2028 interim and a final report with possible law changes by September 15, 2028. The bill includes a $50,000 general fund appropriation and would take effect when passed and approved; the study section would end January 1, 2029.

MT-2027-LC381.s: The bill would let public safety agencies ask former employers for conduct-related information when they do background checks on job applicants. It would require former employers to give that information when asked. It would also limit government liability for these requests and responses.

MT-2027-LC393.s: The bill would change Montana rules for voter registration list checks and address notices. It would require election administrators to use forwardable, first-class confirmation notices when checking voter addresses and handling notices that come back undelivered or get no response. If a voter still does not respond after 30 days, the voter would be moved to the inactive list until the address is verified or the voter updates their registration.

MT-2027-LC398.s: The bill would change the deadlines for several election notices in Montana. It would give election administrators more time to post notices about polling places, absentee ballot counting, and voting system information, and it would require notice to tribal governments. The act would take effect when approved.

MT-2027-LC399.s: The bill would require only state executive branch offices with essential election duties to be open on state general election day. It would change the state rule on office hours for those offices and would take effect on July 1, 2027. It would also require the secretary of state to send a copy of the act to each federally recognized tribal government in Montana.

MT-2027-LC400.s: The bill would revise how the Youth Voting Act is funded. It says public money could not be used for the youth voting program, except for staff time from the secretary of state and the superintendent of public instruction, and it would allow a nonprofit to ask for private donations only for that program. It would take effect right away when passed and approved.

MT-2027-LC420.s: The bill would remove the end date on the rules that let retired teachers work and earn a set amount without a cut in their retirement benefits. It would affect retired members of the teachers' retirement system who take reportable jobs after retirement. The act would take effect on July 1, 2027.

MT-2027-LC447.s: The bill would set up a statutory appropriation, which lets the Department of Justice spend money for the statewide public safety communications system without a separate yearly budget step. It would also move money into the state account for that system, including $5.33 million for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2027, and $5.23 million each year from July 1, 2028, through June 30, 2035. The act would take effect July 1, 2027.

MT-2027-LC450.s: The bill would let a resort area district board create a targeted economic development district and use tax increment financing, which is a way to use future tax growth for project costs. It would require the board to get an infrastructure deficiency report and adopt a development plan that explains the needed fixes and how the money would be used. The rules would apply to resort area districts and would take effect when the act is approved.

MT-2027-LC514.s: The bill would change who can certify a person for a permit to hunt from a vehicle, and it would let more kinds of health care providers do that certification. It would also update the disability rules for hunting and fishing licenses, including the names and definitions used in the law. The act would take effect as soon as it is passed and approved.

MT-2027-LC541.s: The bill would change Montana school finance law to remove the rule that the superintendent of public instruction must print budget forms for school districts. Districts would still use the budget form set by the superintendent. The act would take effect right away when approved.

MT-2027-LC551.s: The bill would change the rules for Montana’s school funding interim commission. It would require the commission to be formed in the 2027-2028 interim and then every 6 years, and it would direct the commission to seek input from parents and students. It would also clarify the commission’s duties and provide an appropriation, which is money set aside for the work.

MT-2027-LC588.s: The bill would revise state definitions for bison and buffalo in Montana’s livestock slaughter laws. It would add buffalo to the list of animals covered in rules for inspectors, slaughter checks, and separate handling of equine meat. It would also change the livestock definition so buffalo and domestic bison are named together in the meat laws.

MT-2027-LC701.s: The bill would set aside state money for noxious weed programs starting July 1, 2027. It would fund early response work, public education and training, biocontrol coordination, weed control on state-owned land, research, and weed data work. The money would come from the marijuana state special revenue account and go to the Department of Agriculture.
